Panton-Valente leucocidin (PVL) is a toxin produced by certain strains of the bacterium Staphylococcus aureus, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). While MRSA is commonly associated with skin infections and hospital-acquired infections, PVL-positive S. aureus has been linked to bacteraemia in patients in the UK.

Studies have shown that approximately 1.6% of S. aureus strains from bacteraemic patients in the UK are PVL-positive. This low incidence suggests that PVL-positive S. aureus are not typically associated with causing serious infections, such as sepsis or necrotizing fasciitis.

However, it is essential to note that the presence of PVL does not necessarily mean that an individual will develop severe infection from this toxin. Some studies suggest that even in individuals without a history of allergies, exposure to PVL-positive S. aureus can trigger allergic reactions.

In summary, while PVL-positive S. aureus are associated with bacteraemia in the UK, it is not typically a pathogenic agent causing serious infections. The presence of PVL may indicate an increased risk for certain individuals or situations, but more research is needed to fully understand its significance.
